 Match Preview News 
 Melbourne Victory visit Auckland FC in Matchweek 5 of the A-League Men. 
 For the second time in the 2026/27 season, having visited Wellington Phoenix for their curtain-raiser, the Boys in Blue cross the Tasman Sea for a trip to New Zealand’s North Island in pursuit of their first three points on Saturday, November 21, kick-off 3:00pm AEDT.
 It is Victory’s first outing in a fortnight, since they were denied a win away to Adelaide United at the death, a result which came a day after this weekend’s opposition, Auckland, dropped points for the first time in a Kiwi Classico.
 Supporters can watch the team’s last league outing of the month at Go Media Stadium live on Paramount+ .
 The Boys in Blue 
 The final FIFA Men’s international window of the year came at an opportune time for Melbourne Victory, following a streak of five matches in two weeks, which continued their busy start to life under Giovanni Savarese’s stewardship.
 Balancing the rigours of both domestic and continental competition is no easy feat, but qualification to the next stage of the AFC Champions League Two remains viable, and whilst the feeling was certainly disappointment upon the long-awaited sound of the full-time whistle in South Australia, only one defeat has been suffered in the A-League Men. 
 This came at the hands of early pacesetters Wellington Phoenix, with the response being three straight score draws, meaning the ACL Two clash in Bandung is Victory’s only scoreless outing this term. And their effort in the final third has been aided by the blossoming Jordi Valadon, who backed up his stunning equaliser against Central Coast Mariners with a thunderstruck go-ahead goal in the Original Rivalry.
 MW5 squad: 1. Jack WARSHAWSKY, 3. Jason DAVIDSON, 5. Brendan HAMILL, 6. Louis D’ARRIGO, 8. Jordi VALADON, 9. Harrison SAWYER, 10. Denis GENREAU, 11. Clerismario SANTOS RODRIGUES, 14. Matthew GRIMALDI, 15. Thomas LOCKYER, 18. Franco LINO, 19. Oliver DRAGICEVIC, 21. Guillermo MAY, 22. Xavier STELLA, 23. Keegan JELACIC, 25. Jack DUNCAN, 26. Jack MIHAILIDIS, 29. Michael GHOSSAINI, 36. Harrison SHILLINGTON, 44. Charles NDUKA.
 Ins: 21. Guillermo MAY (return from injury), 36. Harrison SHILLINGTON (return from suspension).
 Outs: N/A.
 Unavailable: 4. Philipp ZIEREIS (suspended), 16. Joshua INSERRA (injury).
 Injury report. 
 Last time out 
 A 99th-minute equaliser forced 10-player Melbourne Victory to a draw in a Sunday evening Original Rivalry clash at Coopers Stadium.
 A second-half turnaround from Jordi Valadon and Keegan Jelacic, each scoring their second goal of the A-League season, overturned Brody Burkitt’s close-range conversion on the stroke of half-time.
 However, a late red card shown to Philipp Ziereis, combined with 10 minutes of injury time, boosted Adelaide, who squeezed a late leveller through substitute Joey Garuccio.
 Auckland FC failed to beat rivals Wellington Phoenix for the first time in a rain-delayed match in New Zealand’s capital.
 The visitors had notable chances in a slow-burn first half at Go Media Stadium, but the Black Knights came nearest to a winner after the restart.
 Striker Sam Cosgrove twice went close, being kept out by Henry Gray, who also stopped Lachlan Brook at close quarters, and hitting the side netting from a header before the last chance was slid wide in the final knockings by Logan Rogerson.
